name: stat-tile
title: Stat Tile
description: One headline number with its label, change and optional trend line.

examples.title: Stat tile
examples.description: Value with a signed change against last month.

examples.name: stat-tile-grid
examples.title: Grid with sparklines
examples.description: A StatTileGroup where lower is better for two of the figures.

examples.title: Captions, icons and variants

props.name: value
props.description: The figure, already formatted (currency, units, compact notation).

props.name: delta
props.description: Change as a fraction: 0.064 → +6.4%. Shown as a pill with a trend icon.

props.name: deltaLabel
props.description: What the change is measured against, e.g. "vs last month".

props.name: positiveIsGood
props.description: Whether an increase is good news. false for costs, churn, wait times.

props.name: caption
props.description: A quiet line under the value, used instead of a delta.

props.name: icon
props.description: Decorative icon at the top inline-end.

props.name: sparkline
props.description: Recent values, oldest first (≥2 finite points). Decorative line with a 12% area fill and an end dot.

props.name: variant
props.description: Same chrome options as Card; ghost for tiles inside a card.

props.name: children
props.description: StatTiles. Rendered as one <dl> in a responsive grid (~224px minimum per column).

notes: Standalone, a tile is a <dl> (label = <dt>, value and change = <dd>); inside StatTileGroup the group is the <dl> and each tile a <div>.
Good or bad change is shown by colour, a trend icon and the sign — never colour alone.
The delta uses a true minus (−) and is isolated in the locale's direction, so "+6.4%" never renders as "6.4%+" on right-to-left pages.
The sparkline is aria-hidden; put anything that matters in the value, delta or caption. It mirrors on right-to-left pages, with the trend icon.

do: Name the comparison period in deltaLabel.
Set positiveIsGood={false} for metrics where down is good.
Format the value with Intl for the user's locale before passing it.
dont: Don't put more than one number in value.
Don't use the sparkline as the only evidence of a trend.
